sentences.text: Ambopteryx was a scansoriopterygid dinosaur, a group of small theropods, that lived during the Late Jurassic period.
This tiny creature measured only 32 centimeters in length and weighed 306 grams, with its head, neck, and shoulders covered in dense feathers.
Its forelimbs were approximately 1.3 times longer than its hindlimbs, featuring an ulna that was shorter than the humerus but nearly twice as wide as the radius.
Ambopteryx is the second dinosaur known to possess both feathers and bat-like membranous wings.
The genus name combines Latin and Greek roots meaning 'both' and 'wing,' directly referencing this unique combination of structures.
Fossil evidence from its abdominal region reveals the presence of gastroliths and large bone fragments, suggesting it swallowed stones to aid digestion.
The holotype specimen, cataloged as IVPP V24192, was recovered in 2017 from the Haifanggou Formation near Wubaiding Village in Liaoning Province, China.
This specimen belongs to the Yanliao Biota and consists of an articulated, nearly complete skeleton with preserved soft tissue displayed on slabs.
Paleontologists interpret this specific individual as either a sub-adult or an adult based on its development.
Based on unusual dental morphology and stomach contents, scientists suggest Ambopteryx was an omnivore.
Taxonomically, Ambopteryx is classified within the family Scansoriopterygidae.
This dinosaur lived approximately 160 million years ago during the Oxfordian stage of the Late Jurassic in what is now Asia.
The estimated time range for the genus spans from 161.5 to 143.1 million years ago.
